relations.rationale: Jun carrying tea has no bearing on Hugo's height.
Jun carrying tea has no bearing on when Hugo's height becomes obvious.
Jun carrying tea has no logical connection to Finn explaining the Sicilian Defense.
Carrying tea is unrelated to the room's smell of chalk and old wood.
Jun carrying a notebook of opening lines has no direct bearing on Finn explaining the Sicilian Defense.
Jun's notebook is unrelated to Gia noting the smell while locking up.
Rosa's class placement has no bearing on Hugo admiring wooden chess pieces.
If Rosa is in the same class as Finn, and Finn is in the same class as Jun, this supports Rosa also being in Jun's class transitively.
If Rosa is in the same class as Finn, and Finn is in Jun's class, this contradicts the claim that Rosa is not in Jun's class.
Finn bringing the new wooden pieces provides the object that Hugo then admires, directly supporting that claim.
Finn bringing new pieces has no clear bearing on the club setting a future meeting date.
Hugo admiring the pieces doesn't imply he took photographs; these are separate activities.
Hugo taking photographs doesn't affect whether he is the tallest.
If Hugo took the photographs, he likely wasn't in the lineup being photographed, which could contradict the idea that his height stood out in the photo.
Hugo taking photographs is unrelated to Gia and Finn's blitz match.
Gia being a year older than Jun supports the idea that they have an age difference which they forget when arguing.
Gia's age relative to Jun has no bearing on her practicing blitz with Finn.
Gia's age relative to Jun doesn't affect Jun's tournament ranking.
Gia and Jun's age-related arguments have no bearing on Rosa's class placement relative to Jun.
Gia and Jun's arguments about endgame theory and age have no bearing on Hugo's height.
